subsystems.name: Qubit lattice
subsystems.role: a hexagonal (honeycomb) layout where every physical qubit sits on a vertex and couplers run along the edges.
parts: boundary qubits that host logical operators

subsystems.name: Measurement scheduler
subsystems.role: drives the repeating six-step cycle of two-qubit Pauli measurements that defines the code.
parts: cycle pattern of ZZ, XX and YY pair measurements

subsystems.name: Syndrome pipeline
subsystems.role: converts raw measurement outcomes into detector events.

subsystems.name: Decoder
subsystems.role: tracks how the stabiliser group rotates each round and infers the most likely error.

subsystems.name: Logical interface
subsystems.role: exposes encoded qubits and the operations that act on them.
parts: code deformation or lattice-surgery routines for gates

subsystems.name: Verification stack
subsystems.role: proves the code behaves as designed before hardware exists.

buildSteps.title: Lay out the lattice
buildSteps.detail: Place one qubit per vertex of a hexagonal lattice and provide couplers only between nearest neighbours, including the correct boundary shapes.

buildSteps.title: Choose the measurement cycle
buildSteps.detail: Define the repeating sequence of weight-two Pauli measurements (for example alternating ZZ, XX and YY patterns) that returns to its starting point after six rounds.

buildSteps.title: Prove logical invariance
buildSteps.detail: Show mathematically that the logical subspace is mapped back onto itself after each full cycle, so an encoded qubit survives even though the code space keeps changing.

buildSteps.title: Design the decoder
buildSteps.detail: Work out how the stabiliser group rotates between rounds, build the corresponding detector graph, and find an efficient way to decode it — matching-based or automorphism-based.

buildSteps.title: Simulate under noise
buildSteps.detail: Run the schedule through a circuit-level noise model with imperfect gates, measurements and idling, and plot logical error rate against lattice size to estimate a threshold.

buildSteps.title: Compile onto hardware
buildSteps.detail: Map the lattice to the real connectivity of a processor, schedule the measurements within coherence limits, and confirm that mid-circuit measurement and reset work at the required fidelity.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate one logical qubit
buildSteps.detail: Run the cycle on a few tens of physical qubits and look for the signature of error correction: logical error rate falling as the lattice grows.

buildSteps.title: Scale to a logical processor
buildSteps.detail: Add code deformation or lattice-surgery operations so several encoded qubits can be entangled, then repeat the whole schedule for many logical qubits.

prerequisites.why: the code is measurement-only, so every round depends on fast, high-fidelity measurement and re-preparation of qubits.

prerequisites.tech: Low-crosstalk qubit arrays with pair connectivity
prerequisites.why: a hexagon lattice needs clean two-qubit couplings and low idle error on all the qubits that are not being measured.
corrections must be computed within the cycle time as the code space rotates.
Floquet codes are analysed with the same tools — anyon models, thresholds and distance scaling.
the lattice is larger than most current demonstrations, so wafer-scale or modular devices with uniform yield are needed.

pathway.milestone: Floquet codes proposed in 2021 as measurement-only codes with weight-two checks
pathway.unlocks: a route to error correction on hardware where entangling gates are the weakest link.

pathway.milestone: small-device experiments that run the full periodic schedule and watch the logical qubit survive many cycles
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the rotating code space behaves as predicted under real noise.

pathway.milestone: a single logical qubit whose error rate falls as the lattice grows
pathway.unlocks: fault-tolerant memory on hardware that does not need stabiliser-preparation circuitry.

pathway.milestone: logical gates via code deformation and several logical qubits on one chip
pathway.unlocks: a fault-tolerant architecture that can compete with, or complement, the surface code.
